title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: A dazzling, tragic portrait of the American Dream set on the lawns of West Egg, where Jay Gatsby throws lavish parties in pursuit of a love that may never be his. Fitzgerald's prose is a perfect green light glittering across the bay.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Through the eyes of young Scout Finch, Harper Lee's Pulitzer-winning novel unfolds in a sleepy Alabama town where her father, the lawyer Atticus, defends a Black man accused of a crime he did not commit.

author: George Orwell
description: In a future ruled by the Party and watched by Big Brother, Winston Smith begins to keep a forbidden diary. Orwell's nightmare of total control has only grown sharper with every passing decade.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Elizabeth Bennet meets the proud Mr. Darcy and what follows is the most beloved comedy of manners in the English language.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: A small, quiet hobbit named Bilbo Baggins is swept into a journey across mountains and shadow toward a dragon's hoard. Tolkien's opening chord of Middle-earth, played with warmth and wonder.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: On the desert planet of Arrakis, the boy Paul Atreides will become something more than human. Herbert's monumental novel of ecology, religion, and empire still towers over the science-fiction landscape.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A shepherd boy named Santiago dreams of a treasure buried near the Egyptian pyramids and sets out to find it. A modern fable about listening to your heart and reading the omens along the road.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: From wandering apes to architects of nations and machines, Harari traces the surprising story of how Homo sapiens came to rule the earth and reshape it. Sweeping, provocative, unforgettable.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: Tiny changes, remarkable results. Clear distills the science of behavior change into a system of small, compounding habits that quietly reshape a life over months and years.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: Raised in the Idaho mountains by survivalist parents, Tara Westover did not set foot in a classroom until she was seventeen. A luminous memoir about the price and promise of an education.

title: Where the Crawdads Sing
author: Delia Owens
description: For years, rumors of the Marsh Girl have haunted Barkley Cove. When a young man is found dead, the lonely, fiercely intelligent Kya Clark becomes the prime suspect. A mystery wrapped in a love letter to nature.

title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
description: Between life and death there is a library, and within that library, the shelves go on forever. Nora Seed steps inside to read the life she might have lived.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: A lone astronaut wakes up on a spaceship with no memory of how he got there or why. From the author of The Martian, a science-soaked thriller about friendship across the unlikeliest of distances.

title: The Song of Achilles
author: Madeline Miller
description: The story of Achilles, told by the gentle prince who loved him. Miller reimagines Homer's heroes with aching tenderness and the warm Aegean light shining off every page.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
description: Banished to a remote island, the witch Circe finds her own power, her own voice, and her place among gods and mortals. A radiant retelling of an old story made entirely new.

title: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
description: In a Kabul of memory and a Kabul of war, two boys grow up bound by friendship and a single, unforgivable moment. Hosseini's debut is a sweeping novel of guilt and redemption.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: Hawking takes us from the Big Bang to black holes, from the arrow of time to the search for a final theory, in prose that makes the cosmos almost touchable.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: The Nobel laureate maps the two systems of the mind — the fast, intuitive one and the slow, deliberate one — and shows how each shapes the choices we don't even know we are making.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: An innkeeper tells the story of his own legend — of music, magic, and a fire that took everything from him. The first volume of a Kingkiller trilogy fans will defend with their lives.

title: Norwegian Wood
author: Haruki Murakami
description: A song on an airplane sends Toru Watanabe back to a Tokyo of melancholy autumns, of Naoko and Midori, of all the choices love asks of us.

title: Mrs Dalloway
author: Virginia Woolf
description: A single June day in London. Clarissa Dalloway plans a party. Septimus Warren Smith hears the birds in Greek. Woolf gathers a whole life into the hours between morning and evening.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
description: Sethe has escaped slavery, but the past has followed her into the small house on Bluestone Road. Morrison's Pulitzer-winning novel is a haunting in every sense.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
description: Holden Caulfield wanders New York with a red hunting cap and a head full of phonies.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
description: A father and son walk through the ash of the world toward a coast they may never reach. McCarthy strips language down to bone and finds, somehow, that there is still love beneath it.
